I have farmed this 5 mu land for 26 years. Last year I planted spring maize with kidney beans in between the wide rows, same as my neighbor Lao Wang. My maize made about 500 kg per mu and the beans about 120 kg per mu. This year I will do the exact same thing because I know it works and a bad harvest would be a disaster for my family.

I will buy hybrid maize seed from the dealer in town. Two years ago I switched from my own saved seed to hybrid and the yield jumped by nearly 100 kg per mu, so now I pay the extra money without hesitation. For the kidney beans, I will use the improved big-red-seed variety I got from Dealer Zhang last year. My wife says these beans cook softer and the buyer at the market pays two jiao more per jin for them.

Before planting in late April, I will run the rotary tiller through the field twice to break up the soil. Then I will spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — 50 kg of the 15-15-15 kind — as base fertilizer for the whole field. When the maize grows to the big trumpet stage in June, I will spread another 15 kg of urea per mu on the maize rows. I figure that gives the maize about 14 kg of nitrogen per mu in total, and about 6 kg each of phosphorus and potassium from the compound bag. The kidney beans catch some of the base fertilizer that falls near their rows, about half a bag per mu worth, but I do not give them urea because beans make their own nitrogen. That gives them about 4 kg nitrogen per mu and 3 to 4 kg each of phosphorus and potassium.

I have a well, so I will irrigate three times: right after planting in April, again when the maize is jointing in June, and once more when the grain is filling in August. The beans drink at the same time since they are in the same field. For pesticides, I spray herbicide once after sowing to kill the weeds, then insecticide once for the maize stem borers and twice for the bean pod borers. Last year the pod borers ate too many beans so I will not skip the second spray.

I need the maize to yield at least 550 kg per mu and the beans 150 kg per mu to cover my fertilizer, seed, and pesticide costs. My son sends some money from his factory job in Shijiazhuang, but fertilizer prices keep going up, so every yuan matters. I would rather spend an extra 30 yuan per mu on fertilizer than risk losing even 50 kg of yield.
